title: Implement Levenshtein edit distance in Rust using dynamic programming
description: Greenfield Rust task: implement edit_distance(s1: &str, s2: &str) -> usize that returns the minimum number of single-character edits (insertions, deletions, substitutions) needed to transform s1 into s2.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement edit_distance in src/lib.rs.

pub fn edit_distance(s1: &str, s2: &str) -> usize

Algorithm (Wagner-Fischer DP):
- Convert s1 and s2 to char vectors.
- Build (m+1) x (n+1) DP table where dp[i][j] = edit distance between s1[..i] and s2[..j].
- Base cases: dp[i][0] = i, dp[0][j] = j.
- Transition:
  if s1[i-1] == s2[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]
  else: dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])

All 5 tests in tests/edit_test.rs must pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: DP table of size (m+1) x (n+1) initialized with base cases
Diagonal copy when characters match; 1 + min(del, ins, sub) otherwise
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
